An expert's intuition is an alternative, higher-bandwidth but opaque projection. If both systems simply apply the same lossy projection, their divergence is nominal and panel success is mere compliance. Genuine reliability gain occurs only when the checklist corrects a systematic intuition error. Thus, within a single evaluation, one must construct or identify items where the expert intuitively errs but the checklist's explicit steps force the correct verifiable outcome. Observing the panel succeed precisely on these 'trap' items\u2014while the expert fails\u2014proves the checklist is capturing orthogonal signal, not merely riding the same subspace.
